command: search --split validation --budget 512 --seed 42 per condition; 51 validation sources, two archives each; copy analysis per source
note: Chance onset precision toward a source equals its onset density (~.77 mean), so precision is informative only relative to that; Jaccard of the best elite and the best-exceeds-best-human count are the primary indicators. Quality values and QD scores are NOT comparable across conditions.
findings: The v1 scorer is invalid as a search objective: MAP-Elites finds synthetic elites outscoring the best real human tap in 46/51 sources (random search 38/51), consistent with the microtiming exploit.

Removing the offset channel reduces exploitation to 35/51 (random 21/51); adding an onset term reduces it much further (expected 18/51, source 14/51; random 2/51 and 4/51): the onset term makes arbitrary synthetic candidates harder to score highly, increasing robustness relative to humans within the 512-evaluation budget.

The onset terms increase structural copying of the best elite: mean Jaccard of the best elite rises from .21 (v1) / .27 (no_offset) to .38 (expected) / .37 (source). Copy pressure moved from timing exploitation to onset-set imitation.

MAP-Elites exploits every scorer more than matched-budget random search; the gap (e.g., 18 vs 2 under the expected term) measures optimization pressure against the scorer and will grow with budget. The static battery remains the sharper copy test: the source term showed 23/51 copy dominance there despite 14/51 here.

No condition is a trustworthy search objective yet. The expected term currently balances the axes best (static copy 11/51, search exploitation 18/51, retrieval .260/.565) but all step-4 outputs remain synthetic candidate pairings pending human evaluation.
limitations: Single seed and budget; validation sources only; raw-quality comparisons are within-scorer; no human perceptual judgment; no model promoted.
